rag.question: Why is the sky blue?
rag.answer: The sky appears blue because air molecules scatter shorter wavelengths of sunlight more than longer ones (redder light) [2]. This scattering process is also responsible for diffuse sky radiation, where solar radiation is scattered by molecules or particulates in the atmosphere [1]. The blue color of the sky is a result of this selective scattering of light, with blue light (shorter wavelength) being more strongly scattered than red or green light [1].
